speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. Do you experience any abdominal bloating, early satiety, or feeling full quickly when eating? Also, have you noticed any changes in your urine or stool, or any new onset of shortness of breath?

speaker: Doctor
text: I need to evaluate the adnexal mass and the source of bleeding more closely. Have you noticed any abdominal distension or a sensation of pressure in your lower abdomen? Additionally, do you have a family history of breast, ovarian, or colon cancer?

speaker: Doctor

speaker: Doctor
text: The ultrasound shows a thickened endometrial stripe and an adnexal mass, which raises concern for malignancy. To assess for metastasis and tumor markers, I will request a CA-125 blood test and a CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis. REQUEST TEST: CA-125, CT_Abdomen_Pelvis

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal CA-125 and CT findings make advanced ovarian cancer less likely, but the thickened endometrium requires direct evaluation. I will request an endometrial biopsy to rule out endometrial carcinoma. REQUEST TEST: Endometrial_Biopsy

speaker: Doctor
text: The endometrial biopsy confirms well-differentiated adenocarcinoma, which is the primary source of your bleeding. The adnexal mass may represent a synchronous ovarian tumor or metastasis, but the endometrial cancer diagnosis is definitive. DIAGNOSIS READY: Endometrial Adenocarcinoma
